The second SMILES: FC1CN(Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2)C1. That seems to be a fragment containing a fluorine and a CCl substituent. The original side chain had Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3. The template likely breaks a C-Cl bond? Actually the second fragment has CCl attached to phenyl. So the template likely disconnects the side chain at a C-Cl bond, generating a chlorophenyl fragment and a fluorinated azetidine? Wait second SMILES: FC1CN(Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2)C1. That's a fluorinated azetidine (four-membered ring) attached to a benzyl with CCl. So the template gave two fragments: core amide with heterocycle (triazine?) and side chain fragment.

Now we need to apply next template 1914394 to one of the fragments? The order must be 1914393, then 1914394, then 1914395. Likely each step further disconnects each fragment until simple precursors.

We need to produce a retrosynthesis tree with at least 3 reactions, using those templates in order.

First reaction (template 1914393) splits target into two precursors: A = COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nn[nH]c2N)c1 (call fragment A) and B = FC1CN(Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2)C1 (fragment B).
